title: Draft customer-facing Throughput SLO language for Dedicated (contracts + public docs)
creator: Lauren Bishop
description:
We need contract/order-form language and a public-docs-friendly explanation for Dedicated Throughput SLOs that is (a) unambiguous, (b) consistent with SRE’s canonical metric definition, (c) defensible with explicit exclusions, and (d) operationally supportable (escalations + credits). This ticket owns the customer-facing wording and review checklist (Legal + CS + SRE) and will be used by Sales Enablement and in MSA/order-form addenda.

Scope:
- Draft SLO clause text for Order Form / Service Schedule (Dedicated)
- Define measurement/attribution in plain language (what we measure, where, and over what window)
- Define conditions/exclusions (customer throttling, unsupported model/version changes, misuse patterns, scheduled maintenance, warmup, customer-side network issues)
- Define remedies (service credits) and process (how to claim, required evidence)
- Provide a public docs version + FAQ that matches the legal language (but not a contract)
- Create review checklist and sign-off list

Out of scope:
- Final pricing numbers (PM-497)
- Hardware shape catalog details (Infra-owned)
- Internal SLO burn-rate alert thresholds (SRE-owned)

Stakeholders: Sofia Mendes (Commercial Counsel), Rachel Kim (Customer Success), Dev Patel (Support Ops), Sean Gallagher (SRE/SLO semantics), Rafael Mendes (SRE incident policy), Stephanie Nguyen / Isabelle Laurent (Sales Ops), Elliot Price (Docs lead).
proposed_customer_facing_language:
DRAFT v0.9 (for Legal review)

1) Definitions
- “Dedicated Deployment” means a Redwood-managed inference deployment provisioned for Customer’s exclusive use under the Dedicated offering, identified by a unique deployment_id.
- “Committed Throughput” means the minimum throughput floor Redwood commits to provide for a Dedicated Deployment, expressed as tokens per second (tok/s) or requests per second (req/s) as specified on the Order Form.
- “Measured Throughput” means the throughput measured by Redwood at the service edge for requests accepted for processing by the Dedicated Deployment.

2) Throughput SLO
Subject to the Conditions and Exclusions below, Redwood will make commercially reasonable efforts to ensure that, during each Measurement Window, the Measured Throughput for each Dedicated Deployment meets or exceeds the applicable Committed Throughput.

3) Measurement
- Measurement Window: 30-minute rolling windows, evaluated continuously.
- Where measured: at Redwood’s service edge / gateway for the Dedicated Deployment.
- What counts: tokens are counted as output tokens generated by the model for accepted requests (including streaming responses), as recorded by Redwood telemetry.
- Aggregation: throughput is evaluated at the Dedicated Deployment level (deployment_id). If Customer uses multiple routes/models under a single deployment, Committed Throughput applies to the deployment in aggregate unless otherwise stated on the Order Form.

4) Conditions and Exclusions
The Throughput SLO does not apply to, and Redwood is not responsible for, any failure to meet Committed Throughput to the extent caused by:
(a) Customer-side limitations or throttling (including Customer-imposed rate limits, request pacing, concurrency caps, or client timeouts) that prevent Customer from sending sufficient load to utilize Committed Throughput.
(b) Customer configuration or usage outside documented guidance, including unsupported context lengths, unsupported model parameters, or unsupported request/response modes as documented for the applicable model and shape.
(c) Customer-requested changes to model, model version, quantization profile, or deployment configuration not reflected in the Order Form, until Redwood confirms the change is supported for the Committed Throughput.
(d) Scheduled maintenance communicated at least 72 hours in advance, emergency maintenance required for security or stability, or force majeure events.
(e) Issues outside Redwood’s reasonable control, including upstream Customer network/provider failures or Customer application errors.

5) Customer obligations (load test / validation)
Upon initial provisioning and on material configuration changes, Customer will reasonably cooperate with Redwood to validate baseline performance (including running a mutually agreed benchmark or load pattern) to confirm the Committed Throughput can be exercised by Customer’s workload.

6) Remedies
If Customer believes Redwood did not meet the Throughput SLO for an eligible Measurement Window, Customer must notify Redwood within thirty (30) days after the end of the applicable billing month, including the deployment_id, approximate timestamps, and any relevant request identifiers. If Redwood confirms a Throughput SLO miss not subject to the exclusions above, Customer will be eligible for a service credit applied to the next invoice, as described in the Dedicated Service Credit Schedule.

7) Sole and exclusive remedy
Service credits under this section are Customer’s sole and exclusive remedy for any failure to meet the Throughput SLO.

NOTES / OPEN ITEMS FOR LEGAL:
- Confirm whether we should phrase as “SLO” vs “SLA” in contract.
- Confirm notice window (30 days) and credit schedule placement (Service Credit Schedule vs Order Form).
- Confirm whether to include a minimum duration for credit eligibility (e.g., 2+ consecutive windows).
public_docs_version:
DRAFT v0.7 (Docs-friendly, non-contractual)

Dedicated Throughput Commitment (How it works)
- Dedicated includes a committed throughput floor for your deployment (shown in Console and on your Order Form).
- We measure throughput at the deployment level using Redwood telemetry. Throughput is evaluated over rolling 30-minute windows.
- Your committed throughput applies when you are sending enough traffic to use it. If your client throttles requests or stops sending load, we may observe lower throughput that is not attributable to Redwood.

What we measure
- Output tokens generated by the model for requests accepted by your Dedicated deployment (including streaming output).

When a throughput miss can happen
- Capacity/infra issues in the Dedicated pool, regressions impacting a specific model version, or routing/admission-control incidents.

Common reasons a miss is not eligible
- Client-side rate limiting/timeouts, unsupported context lengths, or changing models/versions without confirming performance for your commitment.

If you think you’re below commitment
- Open a support ticket with your deployment_id and time range. We’ll confirm whether it was an eligible SLO miss and share next steps (including credits, if applicable).

This page explains how our commitment is measured; your Order Form and contract govern the actual commitment and remedies.
review_checklist:
Review checklist (must be completed before GA enablement):

SRE/SLO semantics (Sean Gallagher / Rafael Mendes)
- [ ] Metric matches canonical definition (edge-measured, accepted requests only)
- [ ] Measurement windows match SLO tooling (30-min rolling windows)
- [ ] Streaming token accounting described consistently with current implementation
- [ ] Multi-route / multi-model attribution phrasing is correct (deployment-level default)
- [ ] Exclusions do not create operational ambiguity for oncall

Infra/Fleet (Irene Choi / Vanessa Ortiz)
- [ ] Language does not imply unlimited burst or unlimited model flexibility
- [ ] Constraints around shapes/model support are referenced as “documented guidance” and/or Order Form

Support/CS (Dev Patel / Rachel Kim)
- [ ] Ticket intake requirements are clear (deployment_id, timestamps, request IDs)
- [ ] Escalation expectations match playbook and paging policy
- [ ] Customer comms are aligned (what we can/can’t promise)

Legal (Sofia Mendes)
- [ ] SLO vs SLA terminology decision documented
- [ ] Force majeure / maintenance language consistent with master terms
- [ ] Remedy section aligned with credit schedule + limitation of liability
- [ ] Claims window and evidence requirements acceptable

Sales Ops / Enablement (Isabelle Laurent / Stephanie Nguyen)
- [ ] No promises that conflict with tier entitlements (Standard/Plus/Premium)
- [ ] Wording supports quoting without custom one-off edits
- [ ] Any negotiation “give” items identified (e.g., claims window, reporting cadence)

Docs (Elliot Price)
- [ ] Public docs version explicitly non-contractual
- [ ] FAQ covers top questions: burst vs committed, model changes, how to measure, credits
acceptance_criteria:
1) A contract-ready clause draft exists for Dedicated Throughput SLO with explicit definitions, measurement, exclusions, and remedies.
2) A public docs variant exists and is consistent (no contradictions) with the contract language.
3) Review checklist is completed with explicit sign-off notes from Legal + SRE + CS.
4) Language references tier entitlements without hardcoding numbers (numbers live in Order Form / tier sheet).
5) Open questions are resolved or called out as “negotiation points” with guardrails.
rollout_plan:
Rollout plan (language + enablement):
- Internal preview: circulate draft to stakeholders + Sales Enablement for feedback.
- Limited beta: use language in 1–2 Dedicated renewals / new deals (e.g., AlphaBank, HyperDoc) under Legal supervision.
- GA: publish docs page + update order form template and Deal Desk checklist.
- Post-GA: review first 30 days of support tickets for confusion; iterate FAQ wording and intake template.
comments: 2025-02-07 (Lauren Bishop): Creating this because multiple enterprise deals are asking for “throughput guarantee in writing.” Need a single canonical clause so we stop ad hoc edits. Pulling in Sofia + Rachel + Sean for review.

2025-02-12 (Sofia Mendes): Please separate (1) commitment language (what we do) from (2) measurement mechanics (how we measure) and (3) remedy mechanics (credits). Also: avoid “guarantee” wording in the clause header; use “Service Level Objective” unless we explicitly want SLA posture for Premium.

2025-02-14 (Rachel Kim): Support needs a clear intake template. Customers will report “slow” but not provide load details. Add explicit exclusion for customer not sending enough load to utilize the commit, and add a requirement to include deployment_id + time range.

2025-02-18 (Sean Gallagher): Metric note: we should say “requests accepted for processing” vs “requests received,” and be careful with token definition. Output tokens only is fine for throughput; but say we use Redwood telemetry as source of truth. Rolling 30-min window matches evaluator.

2025-02-20 (Lauren Bishop): Updated draft with explicit accepted-request language + 30-min rolling windows, and clarified that multi-route/multi-model defaults to deployment-level unless Order Form states otherwise. Added scheduled maintenance and force majeure exclusions per Sofia’s note.

2025-02-26 (Dev Patel): Add a sentence that customer must notify within X days and provide identifiers. Otherwise we’ll have months-later disputes. Also align with the escalation playbook: CS triage first, then SRE/Infra if eligible miss is likely.

2025-03-03 (Isabelle Laurent): Sales needs an “allowed promises” snippet. If contract says deployment-level aggregate, AEs shouldn’t promise per-route tok/s. Make sure cheat sheet and this clause don’t conflict.

2025-03-06 (Lauren Bishop): Marking In Review. Pending: Sofia final edits + decide SLO vs SLA naming for Premium, and whether to require consecutive windows for credits (to avoid gaming with short dips).
